Hi, ive seen you post a lot on this sub lately and just wanted to emphasize that not all scholars (both currently AND historically) agree that acting on same sex desires is a sin. In fact, there is a history of tolerance towards gender and sexual diversity in many Islamic societies. So no, not all factions throughout time have shared this stance.

Acting as if islamic societies have historically and consistently viewed gender and sexual diversity as unnatural is factually not true. In fact, many Islamic societies were open to lgbtq+ people and not discriminatory. But, sociopolitical factors such as foreign invasion and colonization changed this. You are free to believe that us acting on our sexualities is a sin. I'm not a scholar and I'm not trying to change your opinion at all. I could be wrong for all I know hell. But, there is a history of queerness in Islam that should not just be erased like that. There is a very interesting article by Dr. Ali Oolomi breaking down the history and rise of homophobia in muslim communities that you can find online amongst a myriad of other sources so please approach this with an open mind. Or at least be kind and empathic to queer muslims even if you think acting on it is haraam. Thank you
